headline: Leaders at AI companies are privately rehearsing how to respond to public and political backlash after a major AI-linked disaster, Axios has reported.
score_reason: Pool score kept: notable insider account of industry expectations, but one outlet, anonymous sources and no confirmed event.
importance_line: If an AI-enabled attack hit banking, internet or utilities, the public and lawmakers could react sharply, and the companies are preparing for that, but the report rests on unnamed insiders in one outlet.
summary: Axios reports, as relayed by Yahoo, that leaders at Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI companies are privately planning for the political fallout of a catastrophic AI event, with a large cyberattack on banking, internet, power or water systems the scenario they fear most, and many insiders quoted expect a major incident within six to 12 months. OpenAI said its preparedness exercises "are not treated as inevitable" and Anthropic declined to comment, while the plans reportedly include stress-testing defences and briefing members of Congress ahead of any new rules.
notes: Axios page blocked; text read from Yahoo's report of the Axios scoop. Insiders are unnamed.
